description: The low, crooked birch of the Arctic coast, 3-8 m tall, usually several leaning, twisting stems from one base with dull grey-white bark banded by dark lenticels and a small, wind-shaped crown of little toothed leaves. It makes the only woodland on Lofoten's lower slopes and turns them gold in September.

season_notes.winter: Bare purple-brown twigs over grey-white stems, snow and the polar night.
season_notes.spring: Bare until late May, then catkins and a flush of bright yellow-green, small sticky leaves.
season_notes.summer: Fresh green under the midnight sun; in outbreak years autumnal moth caterpillars strip whole hillsides.
season_notes.fall: Gold in September, bare by mid-October; the leaves blow into the heath.

riparian.water: Not tied to water on the coast (the rain is enough), but the best stands follow the streams and sheltered valley floors.

notes: Grown from white alder (the library's hand-built Betulaceae) as a smaller, multi-stemmed, crooked tree: 2-5 stems leaning 14 degrees with strong curvature, a wind-sheared (asymmetry 0.35) open crown, smooth grey bark (the 'smooth_grey' pattern has the short horizontal lenticels birch shows). COMPROMISES: the generator's lean is random in direction, not downwind, so a stand will not show one prevailing lean; the polycormic, half-prostrate krummholz form at the treeline (stems creeping before turning up) cannot be drawn: the stems all start upright or splayed from the base. Wikipedia: 10-20 m (rarely 27 m) for the species, subarctic specimens usually small and very contorted (var. pumila, formerly subsp. tortuosa), smooth dull grey-white bark with dark horizontal lenticels, leaves ovate 2-5 cm (smaller in the mountain birch), autumnal moth outbreaks defoliating large areas. Lofoten's calendar: polar night in December and early January, birch bare from about October to the end of May, leaf-out in late May and June, autumn yellow in September; the climate is oceanic, winters mild for the latitude, the treeline low (a few hundred metres) under salt wind. Red deer browse it on Lofoten; moose and mountain hare presence on Moskenesoya itself needs local checking (drafter's knowledge); willow ptarmigan eat the buds and catkins in winter. None of these animals is in the library yet. Region tag scandinavia is not yet a natural region in pipeline/regions.py.
